source.citation: Student (1908). The probable error of a mean. Biometrika 6(1), 1–25; data from Cushny and Peebles (1905).

question: Use a two-sided paired t-test to compare the mean within-patient difference drug_2 minus drug_1, in additional hours of sleep.

scope.supports: Modern two-sided reanalysis of the paired historical values; reproduce the published mean difference of 1.58 hours.
scope.does_not_support: A modern randomized clinical trial, current treatment guidance, or an exact reproduction of Student's historical probability wording.

independent_reference.calculation: Independent explicit oracle; no application compute function or LLM

result.tool_call: scipy.stats.ttest_rel(after, before, nan_policy='raise', alternative='two-sided'); confidence_interval(confidence_level=0.95); difference = y minus x
result.pairing_definition: Each included row is one independent pair; x is before and y is after.

numerical_tool_reference.note: Read-only numerical reference call; does not approve the workflow's pending data checks.

retrieved_references.title: Comparing two independent means
retrieved_references.keywords: mean compare difference group independent score 平均 差异 两组
retrieved_references.text: Use a numeric outcome and two independent groups. Welch allows unequal variances. The estimand is a difference in population means, not a causal effect without an appropriate design. A normality test alone does not select or replace the method.

retrieved_references.title: Comparing two measurements on the same subjects
retrieved_references.keywords: paired same before after drug sleep repeated 配对 同一 前后 睡眠
retrieved_references.text: Each row must contain both measurements on one subject; different pairs must be independent. Compare the mean within-pair difference y minus x. The relevant distribution is the differences. Do not treat the two measurements as independent groups or silently remove incomplete pairs.
